translation: First use the manual technique to lift and raise the neck, nape, sinews, and bones; then wrap the head with cloth in two or three layers and make it tight; then use the vibrating stick to pat and strike the soles of the feet lightly, so that the qi of the five viscera (五臟) is opened and communicated above and below, and the stagnant blood is dispersed; then it will not rush to the heart, nor cause vomiting and hiccup, and the mind and spirit will be at ease. If, after the head has been wrapped and the soles of the feet struck, the patient feels no pain at all, is unconscious and unaware of people, the phlegm sounds like dragging a saw, the body is stiff, and saliva and froth flow from the mouth—this is the qi and blood on the verge of exhaustion, and it is not treatable. <ins>Shoulder-covering instrument (披肩器)</ins> (3, no figure) The shoulder-covering instrument is made of a piece of cooked oxhide, five cun (寸) long and three cun wide, with two holes opened at each end. It is clamped over the injured place, and cotton cord is threaded through and bound tightly; compared with a wooden board it is somewhat more pliable and lively.
